brief: Goldman's Prime Book is in a hedge fund de-grossing episode: beta-adjusted net exposure fell 3.5 points on the week and 10.3 on the month to a 1-year low, driven by de-grossing in 7 of the last 8 sessions after META's results sharpened focus on AI financing and return on capital. Net allocation to semis/semicap hit this year's low. Goldman does not read this as overvaluation and recommends selectively buying the AI dip via Power, Hyperscalers, Inference and Cyber, funded by shorting cyclicals (GSXUCYCL) against slowing growth, higher oil prices and tighter financial conditions. Momentum (GSPRHIMO) has erased its YTD gains on a 43% drawdown, but cleaner positioning (lowest since June 2025) makes buying the dip more attractive even as SPXXAI's broadening trade has closed the gap with the S&P 500. Healthcare is flagged as an AI-uncorrelated beneficiary of AI adoption. Separately: UK consumer confidence posted its largest ex-Covid decline since Brexit even as a momentum unwind lifted GSXEUKCO 10%, a move Goldman expects the Autumn Budget, a BoE hike and weak Q3 earnings to reverse; and China's stronger data hasn't drawn risk-taking into equities despite a policy-driven ETF rebound.
